fellowship.projectTitle: Performance characterization of PET detectors and systems
fellowship.projectAbstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) is a major molecular imaging modality that plays a key role at the forefront of medicine. Complementary to anatomical imaging by x-ray and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), PET allows doctors and researchers to examine functions such as metabolism, gene expression, cell proliferation, and drug uptake in a subject. It is useful for studying and diagnosing cancer and neurodegenerative diseases that are fundamentally functional disorders. In this project, through hands-on experiments on PET detectors and systems that have been developed or are under development in Kao’s lab at UChicago, the students will be exposed to the concept and practice of molecular imaging, and learn the basic physical principle, electronics of PET detector, and other performance and practical considerations for PET.
